title: Interface Engineering Boosts Power Conversion Efficiency of MAPbI3 Perovskite Solar Cells
notice: SYNTHETIC example, not real papers. Invented for pipeline demonstration only.

paragraphs.text: We report methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) perovskite solar cells with a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.1% under 1-sun AM1.5G illumination.
Perovskite solar cells have attracted intense interest because certified efficiencies now rival crystalline silicon devices.
Interface recombination at the TiO2/perovskite boundary limits the open-circuit voltage (Voc) of planar devices.
A compact TiO2 electron transport layer was deposited on FTO-coated glass by spray pyrolysis at 450 °C and used as the electron-selective contact.
The MAPbI3 precursor was spin-coated from a DMF solution and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min, followed by a spiro-OMeTAD hole transport layer.
Current density-voltage (J-V) characteristics were recorded with a class-AAA solar simulator at 1-sun AM1.5G.
The champion device achieved a PCE of 21.1%, with a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 23.4 mA/cm2, a Voc of 1.12 V, and a fill factor (FF) of 80.5%.
SnO2-passivated control devices reached only 19.3% PCE under identical 1-sun test conditions.
The hysteresis index was not measured in this study.
We attribute the efficiency gain to suppressed interfacial recombination at the compact TiO2/perovskite interface.
All reported efficiency values are as-fabricated initial performance measured without encapsulation.
Interface engineering delivers efficient MAPbI3 solar cells, but long-term damp-heat stability remains untested here.
